name: crypto-hkdf256
algorithm: std HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869): for every 32-byte input key of splitmix64 bytes, Extract with a 32-byte salt then Expand to 42 bytes with a 12-byte info, the salt's first byte xored with each output's, reps passes (mk/crypto-hkdf256.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard KDF
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no HKDF; the hkdf crate is third-party, and no crate stands in (plan/06-m6.md 4.1)

notes: Work per step: one Extract (one HMAC-SHA256 of 32 bytes under the 32-byte salt) and one Expand to 42 bytes (two HMAC blocks), TLS 1.3's derivation shape: Mk crypto.HkdfExtract and HkdfExpand, Go crypto/hkdf.Extract and Expand, Zig kdf.hkdf.HkdfSha256.extract and expand. Derivations per second = mib * 32768 * reps / median.

SHA-256: Mk and Go use the CPU's SHA extensions when present (Mk through std.simd.kernel's Sha256Blocks, D8-17; Go through its amd64 assembly), Zig at x86_64_v2 is scalar. Labelled: on a CPU with SHA-NI the zig cell compares instruction sets as well as libraries.

Checksums from the go column (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off, Go 1.27, owner's machine, 2026-11-12); the Mk column (mk build --release, mk from the tree) printed the same at both arg sets. Written by the std-crypto2 lane. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
